findings.title: Zero NLP / Semantic Understanding -- Apache Solr q=* Wildcard
findings.expected_behavior: User types 'beach holiday in November under 2,000 GBP' and sees relevant Caribbean/Mediterranean packages ranked by relevance
findings.actual_behavior: Apache Solr fires q=* (wildcard match only) -- zero query understanding. All search logic is structured filter queries. Conversational/NLP queries are architecturally impossible.
findings.prospect_description: BA Holidays runs Apache Solr self-hosted at /solr/hotelPackages/safe. The q=* wildcard is definitive: the system has zero natural language processing. A traveller typing beach in January or ski resort from London gets nothing. The entire discovery model is filter-first, not search-first.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia NeuralSearch replaces Solr as the search layer on top of BA Holidays existing hotel inventory data. NeuralSearch understands beach in November and returns relevant coastal resort packages. No Amadeus Nevio dependency -- pure search-layer swap. Deploys in 90 days.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Search became 'a true strategic lever for growing direct online bookings' -- higher CTRs, more online conversions, fewer zero-result pages, ~10ms response (200x faster than industry benchmark)

findings.title: No Search-as-You-Type (SAYT) / Autocomplete on Destination Fields
findings.expected_behavior: As user types, destination suggestions appear instantly with popular destinations, packages, and price indicators
findings.actual_behavior: No SAYT/autocomplete detected on destination fields. Solr fires batch queries on page load only -- not on individual keystrokes. Customers must type a full airport code or exact destination name.
findings.prospect_description: BA Holidays destination fields trigger Solr batch queries on page load -- not on keystroke. No predictive autocomplete guides the customer. This is one of the highest-friction moments in the booking journey.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Autocomplete with Query Suggestions surfaces destination options, price ranges, and popular packages as the user types -- from the first character.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Higher click-through rates and more online conversions after deploying Algolia Query Suggestions and Recommendations across 35 markets

findings.title: Zero Typo Tolerance -- Misspellings Return No Results
findings.expected_behavior: Typo-tolerant search corrects 'Barcellona' to 'Barcelona' and returns relevant holiday packages
findings.actual_behavior: Solr uses default query parser with q=* wildcard -- no fuzzy matching, no typo correction. Holiday search does not accept free-text at all (pure filter model).
findings.prospect_description: BA holiday search does not process free-text input at all. The real risk is on /travel/searchba/ (vendor unknown) where typo tolerance is unmeasured. With 18.5M monthly visitors and 61.76% on mobile, every unrecovered typo is a lost booking.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia built-in typo tolerance (1 typo per word up to 8 characters, 2 typos above) is on by default -- no configuration required.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: +37% conversion rate, +150% sales contribution from search after deploying Algolia (including typo tolerance and NeuralSearch)

findings.title: No Federated Search -- Three Disconnected Search Systems
findings.expected_behavior: Unified search surfaces relevant results across holidays, flights, help articles, and FAQs in a single interface
findings.actual_behavior: Three completely disconnected search systems: Apache Solr (holidays), Inbenta KM (help/FAQ), unknown vendor (/travel/searchba/ -- blocked). No unified search experience. Help page has no on-page search box.
findings.prospect_description: A BA customer who wants to check baggage allowance before booking a holiday must navigate Header, Accordion category, Subcategory -- with no search box on the help page itself. With NPS as a CEO KPI, this manual navigation is a direct NPS detractor.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia federated search unifies holidays, help content, and page results in a single search bar with categorized results. Customers who self-serve via search do not call centres.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Reduced call-centre dependency and increased direct online conversions after deploying unified Algolia search across 35 markets

findings.title: No Personalization in Holiday Search Results
findings.expected_behavior: A BA Club Gold member sees premium cabin offers and luxury resorts surfaced first; a first-time visitor sees popular value packages
findings.actual_behavior: Results sorted by geo-distance from user IP and total price only. No loyalty tier signal in search ranking. Adobe Target active on holidays page for A/B testing of page content -- but not search result ranking.
findings.prospect_description: The new spend-based British Airways Club (April 2025) requires BA to sell more ancillaries and holiday packages to retain high-value members. Search personalization is the conversion infrastructure that makes the loyalty model succeed.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Personalization connects BA Club tier and travel history data to real-time search ranking -- Gold members see premium cabin and luxury resort offers first. IAG Loyalty GBP 469M profit base grows when members find and book holidays faster.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: +37% conversion rate after deploying Algolia Personalization, Rules, and Analytics

findings.title: Zero Product Recommendations on Holiday Pages
findings.expected_behavior: Below or alongside results: 'Popular this week', 'Trending destinations from London', 'Customers also booked', cross-sell to car hire or airport lounges
findings.actual_behavior: No product recommendations visible anywhere on holiday pages. Baynote (former recommendations engine) listed as removed technology with no confirmed replacement.
findings.prospect_description: BA Holidays has 10,500+ hotels across 600+ destinations. With no recommendations engine, the catalogue is inaccessible beyond explicit filter searches. Baynote was removed and never replaced -- a 5+ year gap in recommendation capability.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Recommend deploys ML-powered recommendations with zero custom ML required.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Club Med deployed Algolia Recommendations alongside Search -- increased online conversions and direct bookings across 35 markets

findings.title: Help Centre Relies on 2018 Inbenta FAQ Chatbot -- No Modern Search
findings.expected_behavior: Instant search results surface the most relevant baggage articles, with typo tolerance and query suggestions
findings.actual_behavior: Inbenta Knowledge Management (purchased 2018) powers help search. Help page has no search box -- customers navigate accordion categories. No NeuralSearch, no dynamic facets, no on-page instant search.
findings.prospect_description: Sean Doyle has NPS as a personal KPI (+10.5 points improvement in FY2025). Help search quality directly drives NPS: customers who cannot find answers via self-service call BA contact centres.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia can replace or complement Inbenta for the help/knowledge centre -- search-as-you-type on baggage allowance surfaces instant results with typo tolerance and federated display.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: Reduced call-centre dependency through improved digital search self-service

findings.title: No Search Analytics or Intelligence Feedback Loop
findings.tested_query: N/A -- analytics signals not visible in search UI
findings.expected_behavior: Search surfaces trending destinations, popular searches, 'people also looked at' -- and analytics feed back to improve ranking automatically
findings.actual_behavior: Zero search analytics signals visible in any tested search surface. Solr self-hosted has no built-in analytics feedback loop. ContentSquare and Quantum Metric track session-level UX but do not feed search ranking.
findings.prospect_description: BA has 18.5M monthly visits and a substantial holiday catalogue. Without search analytics, BA cannot know which destination queries return zero results, which filters are used most, or what causes users to abandon search.
findings.algolia_solution: Algolia Analytics provides real-time search metrics: zero-result rate, click-through rate by query, A/B test results for ranking changes. AI Re-ranking automatically improves result order based on click patterns.
findings.algolia_case_study_result: +37% conversion rate -- analytics-driven ranking optimisation was central to the Lacoste Algolia deployment

No Algolia detected anywhere. Solr is the primary displacement target; /travel/searchba/ is the critical unknown.

touches.subject: Email 1 — HOOK
touches.body:
Hi Jake,

Your CEO told The Register last December that British Airways is "behind the curve" on digital. We decided to check whether that was visible on ba.com — and it is.

We inspected the BA Holidays booking widget live this week. When a customer types a natural-language query — "beach in November," "ski resorts from Gatwick," "romantic break under a thousand pounds" — the destination field fires Apache Solr with `q=*`.
